title: Antarctica: The Frozen Continent
text: Antarctica is Earth's southernmost continent, containing the geographic South Pole. It is the fifth-largest continent and is almost entirely covered by an ice sheet averaging 1.9 km thick, containing about 70% of the world's fresh water. Antarctica is the coldest, driest, and windiest continent, with the lowest recorded temperature of -89.2°C measured at the Soviet Vostok Station in 1983. Unlike the Arctic, Antarctica is a land mass, and it is surrounded by the Southern Ocean. No humans permanently inhabit Antarctica; it is governed by the Antarctic Treaty System, which prohibits military activity and supports international scientific cooperation.
